title: "The Smoke Jumpers": A Juneteenth story about the 555th Parachute Infantry
description: This Juneteenth, we honor the 555th Parachute Infantry Battalion, the "Smoke Jumpers," who in WWII bravely fought Japanese "fire balloon" bombs and wildfires, saving lives and advancing equality. (U.S. Army video by Spc. Elizabeth MacPherson, B-Roll footage from the National Archives Catalog, Music by 'The Epic BadGer')

transcript.text: This June 10th . We honor the
courageous 5 55th parachute infantry
battalion . The army's first
firefighting paratroopers nicknamed the
smoke jumpers activated in world war
two . The first all black airborne unit
expected to fight overseas but the
mission changed when danger arrived at
home , the Japanese had begun launching
thousands of fire balloon bombs on the
Pacific Northwest in Bly Oregon , a
pregnant woman and her five Children
were killed . Civilian lives had been
taken on us soil and somebody had to
make sure it never happened again .
Enter the 5 55th , specially chosen
volunteers of 92nd ID , they assembled
for operation firefly . A secret
mission aimed to destroy the balloons
and suppress forest fires . The 5 55th
parachuted directly into the wildfires
and in the summer of 1945 they executed
over 1000 and jumps and extinguished
nearly 30 fires . The Japanese balloon
bombs had failed and for the rest of
the war , no civilian lives were lost
again on American soil . In 1947 the
smoke jumpers integrated into the 82nd
Airborne Division , bringing the Army
and America one step closer to equality
